_provenance.note: tgId 25, tcId 174 (curve P-256, hashAlg SHA2-256) — the group's sole testPassed=true case among its 7 (the other 6 are deliberate negative cases: modify key, modify r, modify message, zero s, zero r, modify s). qx/qy/r/s are each exactly 32 bytes (canonical P-256 field/order width), so no leading-zero stripping was needed to fit OSSLECDSA::verify's `signature.size() != 2 * orderLen` check or tests/helpers.mjs importECPublicKey's fixed-width point construction. Independently re-verified against Python's cryptography library (49.0.0) before use: EllipticCurvePublicNumbers(qx, qy, SECP256R1()).public_key().verify(encode_dss_signature(r, s), message_bytes, ec.ECDSA(hashes.SHA256())) raised no exception — VALID, matching ACVP's own testPassed=true label. REPLACES a file that carried no _provenance block and declared `"source": "RFC 6979 Appendix A.2.5 (ECDSA P-256, SHA-256, message \"sample\")"` — real published RFC values, but Tier-3 material used where Tier-1 ACVP coverage exists for this exact algorithm/curve/hash, which the remediation plan's §1 ladder does not permit (Tier 1 is mandatory wherever it exists). `message` is 128 bytes of ACVP-generated pseudorandom data (hex-encoded) — NOT literal text like the RFC 6979 vector's "sample" was. tests/acvp-wasm.mjs's ECDSA P-256 block previously passed this field through `new TextEncoder().encode(textMsg)` (literal-text encoding, via the `ecdsaVerify` helper), which only worked because the old vector's message happened to be printable ASCII; a real ACVP message is not. Rewired the call site to hex-decode `msg` and dispatch through the existing generic `verifyBytes(M, hSession, h, hexToBytes(tv.msg), sig, CK.CKM_ECDSA_SHA256)` helper — the same helper already used for the ML-DSA SigVer KAT a few lines below it in the same file — rather than inventing a new encoding path.
